episodes.166919: A line of storms developed across Iowa during the afternoon of Saturday, April 23rd. These storms were moving quickly northward just ahead of a cold front that was moving eastward across Minnesota. As these storms moved into south central Minnesota, isolated damage occurred northeast of Janesville. Several surges along the reflectivity gradient line provided sporadic tree and farm outbuilding damage between Janesville and  Owatonna, northeastward to Red Wing. The strongest circulation was noted south of Cannon Falls, before moving northeastward over the Mississippi River near Red Wing.
episodes.167039: Forcing associated with a system over northern Minnesota/Wisconsin helped generate a round of severe thunderstorms ahead of an attendant cold front moving across the Great Lakes during the afternoon and evening of 4/24. Areas near Saginaw Bay experienced damaging wind gusts with this round of storms, knocking down trees and powerlines across Gladwin, Arenac, and Iosco counties.
episodes.167040: A line of storms with a history of producing damaging wind gusts over northern Michigan moved over the nearshore waters near East Tawas, producing a 55 mph wind gust at the Tawas Point mesonet station.
episodes.167166: A shortwave trough was moving into New Mexico. There was a Pacific front near the I-20 corridor in West Texas and an intersecting dryline that extended southward. The air was unstable with high wind shear along and east of the dryline. These conditions resulted in showers and thunderstorms that developed near the front and dryline. The showers and thunderstorms produced flash flooding and hail in the Permian Basin.
episodes.167522: An isolated severe storm produced wind gusts measured at up to 67 mph in Lansing.
episodes.167660: Scattered severe thunderstorms impacted the Flint vicinity.
episodes.167661: A thunderstorm moving through Saginaw Bay produced a wind gust near 50 knots.
episodes.168168: A line of thunderstorms developed over the area and produced damaging wind gusts in a few counties during the evening of 4/23.
episodes.168322: A dryline positioned itself to the west of the I-35 corridor, with several supercells developing by late afternoon of the 23rd. These storms brough hail and wind to parts of central and southwest Oklahoma, as well as a couple tornadoes.
episodes.168462: Several episodes of heavy rain combined with snowmelt resulted in minor flooding along the Sturgeon River in Houghton County in late April.
episodes.168560: A cold front interacting with a seasonably warm and humid airmass triggered a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms across central Illinois during the afternoon of April 24th.  One of the cells spawned a brief EF-1 tornado northeast of Sharpsburg in Christian County.  Meanwhile other storms produced wind gusts of 50 to 60mph and isolated damage across portions of Sangamon and Christian counties.
episodes.168693: A line of strong thunderstorms produced gale force gusts to the nearshore waters of Racine.
episodes.168710: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a cold front in the early morning hours, with quarter sized hail and a few stronger winds gusts reported in central Iowa around sunrise. This pushed east of the area by mid morning and temperatures warmed. This allowed for deep mixing and non-thunderstorm associated wind gusts of 50 to over 60 mph occurred across the area through the afternoon. In the evening a secondary front passed across the state, with daytime heating allowing for more robust convection to develop. The bowing, linear storm system primarily produced a swath of wind gusts and damage, however a few smaller hail reports were made.
episodes.168892: A slow-moving cold front helped to generate showers and thunderstorms across much of the region. Some storms produced heavy rain along the Red River that resulted in nuisance flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169147: In the evening of April 23, 2022, strong thunderstorms moved into northwest Missouri and northeast Kansas. These storms were primarily wind makers, with scattered 60+ mph reports and some minor damage across the area.

Scattered tree damage was observed southwest of Harrah from just west of Peebly Road on Reno Avenue to northeast of NE 10th Street and Dobbs Road. Although most of the damage showed indications of damaging thunderstorms winds, one area on the northern fringe of the showed signs of a brief tornado from Peebly Road to near the Kickapoo Turnpike (see separate entry for this tornado).

A weak tornado developed just west of Peebly Road north of Reno Avenue and moved northeast. Tree damage was observed along Peebly Road and just west of the Kickapoo Turnpike. This tornado was within a much broader area of wind damage.

A large area of wind damage began just west of NE 63rd Street and Peebly Road, with the damaging wind swath continuing south along and near Peebly Road to near NE 50th Street, then southeast to Luther Road just north of NE 36th Street, then turning east-northeast across the Kickapoo Turnpike to NE 50th Street and Dobbs Road. Winds were generally up to 60-70 mph through much of this region, but localized near 100 mph where a number of power poles were broken along Luther Road north of NE 36th Street.||Embedded within this area of damaging winds, evidence does point to a brief tornado near the beginning of this path. (See separate entry for this tornado).

A weak tornado touched down about 4 miles northwest of Harrah and moved south-southeast near Peebly Road between NE 63rd and NE 50th Streets. Some light tree damages was observed. This was embedded within a much larger area of damaging thunderstorm winds.

Snowmelt combined with periods of heavy rain resulted in minor flooding along the Sturgeon River near Alston in late April.

Thunderstorm wind damage occurred along a 3-mile long, 1/4-mile wide area stretching from west to east along County Road 1580 and Royal Oak Road. An apartment building along Indian Meridian Road had its roof removed by the winds and a mobile home also suffered some roof damage. There were a number of trees damaged within this area. Evidence showed nearly all of the winds within this broad area were from west to east, with the exception of evidence of rotational winds near and east of County Road 3220 (see separate entry for this tornado).

A brief tornado occurred just southwest of Pauls Valley within a much broader area of wind damage. Although much of the damage in the Pauls Valley area indicated straight-line winds blowing from west to east, debris indicated a small area of rotational winds associated with a tornado near the intersection of County Road 3220, and Royal Oaks Road which damaged a salon and pushed farm implements to the west.

Heavy rain fell across Howard County and produced flash flooding in Big Spring. There were multiple reports of homes flooded throughout the city of Big Spring. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A tornado touched down 3 miles east-northeast of Sharpsburg at 5:49 PM CDT.  The tornado demolished a 60 by 120-foot shed along East 1900 North Road just west of North 1300 East Road.  Damage from the shed was thrown about a mile to the east-northeast.  The tornado quickly dissipated 4 miles east-northeast of Sharpsburg at 5:50 PM CDT.
